"While somewhat unrelated (?), I recently asked the President of South Korea if they would like to join us in the Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and they said, ‘No thanks!’" Trump wrote.
Reuters contributed to this report.
Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

title: Spanish journalist says Ceuta residents believe government isn't doing enough to prevent another migrant rush
summary: Ceuta residents say they feel scared after 70,000 migrants flooded Spain's North African enclave, as border security concerns grow amid Morocco tensions.
story: Conservative Spanish journalist Javier Negre reveals that residents of Ceuta, a Spanish enclave bordering Morocco in North Africa, say the Spanish government is not doing enough to prevent another flood of migrants from Morocco.

Residents of Ceuta, Spain's North African enclave bordering Morocco, are saying that the government is not doing enough to prevent another mass immigration event like the July 30 influx of approximately 70,000 migrants into the city, conservative Spanish journalist Javier Negre told Fox News Digital.

"The local citizens, they are really sad. And no matter if they are left or right, What they say is like, it's really complicated to live right now in Ceuta," Negre told Fox News Digital in an interview.
Negre said citizens have cited incidents in which migrants committed crimes, including robbery and attempted rape, adding "they live in the street and the people are really scared."

"We need in Spain, we need in Europe, governments that try to avoid the illegal immigration right now because it's not fair for the citizens that pay taxes to have social security, to have healthcare and these illegal migrants, they collapse the hospitals, they collapsed the universities, the schools, and it's not fair for the Spanish people," Negre said.
STATE DEPARTMENT RAISES TRAVEL WARNING FOR PART OF SPAIN AS MIGRANT SURGE SPARKS MILITARY DEPLOYMENT

Migrants run and cheer as they cross on foot into the North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco, after swimming over from the Moroccan side and overwhelming police at the city's breakwater, according to Spain's Guardia Civil, in Ceuta, Spain, July 30, 2026. (FARO TV via Reuters)

The residents who reportedly spoke to Negre seemingly echoed comments from Juan Jesús Vivas, Ceuta's mayor-president. Speaking during an extraordinary session of the European Parliament's Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs, Vivas said the migrant rush put public safety and public health at risk and threatened to collapse the city's immigration infrastructure.

"Furthermore, the morale of Ceuta's residents is severely affected. Our population feels sad, helpless, uneasy, fearful and worried — and with good reason. It is inevitable to wonder whether this will happen again, and if that next time will be the definitive plunge into the abyss, causing us to cease being what we are: Spain and Europe," Vivas said.

Ceuta President Juan Jesus Vivas seen during a meeting at the Consolat de Mar on Aug. 6, 2026, in Palma, Balearic Islands, Spain. The meeting takes place just one week after the unprecedented migration crisis at the border between Ceuta and Morocco. (Javier Fernandez/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Following a circulation of social media messages in Morocco calling for migrants to again rush the Spanish enclave on Aug. 15, both Spain and Morocco beefed up security on their respective sides of the border, in addition to the maritime barriers Spain put up after the initial incident saw migrants swim ashore.
But, Negre said Moroccan officials told him that the increased measures are not enough.
"I know that today the Spanish government and the Moroccan government, they say that they are going to put more police, but it's not enough," Negre said.

"We need more police," he continued. "We need to have more border security because people don't understand why they're paying taxes, why they're giving a lot of money to the state if they can't block the frontier to these illegal migrants that they are not escaping from a war or a difficult situation," Negre told Fox News Digital.
Escorted by the Spanish army, migrants who crossed into Spain return to Morocco from the Spanish enclave of Ceuta on Aug. 1, 2026. (AP Photo/Antonio Sempere)

Negre criticized Spain's government, led by left-wing Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his party, Vox. The journalist pointed to Spanish media reports arguing that Sánchez's frosty relationship with Morocco may have contributed to the migration incident.

"Pedro Sánchez, who is involved in a lot of scandals of corruption, he went to Algeria, and there are some rumors that maybe the king of Morocco try to promote this illegal invasion to tell the Spanish government, 'hey, take it easy,'" Negre explained.
TRUMP CRITICIZES SPAIN AMID IRAN, NATO RIFT AS PM SANCHEZ FACES QUESTIONS OVER POLITICAL MOTIVES

Sánchez traveled to Algeria on July 20, 10 days before the migration incident, in an effort to restore diplomatic ties after a freeze in the countries' relationship over Morocco's claim to the Western Sahara.
Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez arrives to attend a press conference following a cabinet meeting at the Moncloa Palace in Madrid on March 20, 2026. (Pierre-Philippe Marcou/AFP via Getty Images)

Western Sahara, a desolate region in northwest Africa, has long been the focus of hostile relations between Algeria and Morocco. In 2020, the U.S. officially recognized Morocco's claim of sovereignty over the region.

While Spain does not officially recognize that claim, Sánchez did endorse Morocco's autonomy plan for the region, which proposes limited self-governance under Moroccan sovereignty to be the "most serious, realistic, and credible basis" for resolving a long-standing dispute between Morocco and Algeria over the territory.

Sánchez revealed his decision in a March 2022 letter to Morocco's King Mohammed VI, a letter he sent less than a year after another migrant influx from Morocco into Ceuta. During that May 2021 incident, Moroccan border guards appeared to stand down while 10,000 people flooded into Ceuta from the African nation.
'YOU'RE DESTROYING YOUR COUNTRIES': IS EUROPE FINALLY HEEDING TRUMP'S WARNING ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION?

While Moroccan officials denied they instructed border guards to stand down, the European Parliament passed a resolution condemning Morocco for the incident, citing statements from Morocco's Ministry of Foreign Affairs acknowledging that the incident was retaliation for Spain treating the leader of a Western Saharan rebel group at a Spanish hospital.
A view of the border between Morocco and Algeria, seen from Algeria on Jan. 29, 2026. (Hamza Zait/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Negre also took aim at European leadership writ large, contrasting the European Parliament with President Donald Trump.

"Europe is going really bad with illegal immigration, with the open frontiers, completely opposite as the politics of President Trump with border security and deporting all the illegal migrants," he told Fox News Digital, while praising Trump's proposed legislation to require voter identification, the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, known as the SAVE Act.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Fox News Digital contacted the governments of Spain, Ceuta, Morocco and Algeria for further comment.

title: Father of sailor aboard USS Lincoln detained by immigration authorities, family says
summary: Joshua Aviles said he has been “fighting for a country that has given me everything,” only to learn his father had been detained.
story: The immigrant father of a sailor on board the beleaguered USS Abraham Lincoln was detained Saturday by immigration officials, family members said.
Luis Manuel Aviles, originally from Nicaragua, was detained shortly after 11 a.m. ET in Key West, Florida, where he lives, stepdaughter Katty Delgado told NBC News on Saturday evening.
She said that Aviles has been in the U.S. for roughly 20 years and that she has no knowledge of an arrest history or criminal allegations against him.
“He’s doing everything the right way,” she said.

The Department of Homeland Security confirmed Sunday that the Border Patrol arrested Aviles during a traffic stop in Key West. The agency said Aviles entered the U.S. illegally at an unknown date and location and would remain in ICE custody pending removal proceedings.
“We are simply enforcing the laws passed by Congress. This Administration does not pick and choose which laws to enforce,” a DHS spokesperson said.

Delgado said she learned the news from family members, including Aviles’ wife and his son Joshua Aviles, who posted a note about the detention on Facebook. Her stepfather, Delgado said, was arrested near a Publix supermarket as he was headed to a mechanic.

Joshua Aviles said on Facebook that he’s on board the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, which is on its way back to the U.S. after its prolonged stretch at sea, including its deployment to the Middle East to engage in the war with Iran.
“I’ve been deployed for over nine months, out at sea in the Middle East aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, fighting for a country that has given me everything,” he wrote Saturday.
He said that his father is hard-working, giving and humble and that he has a work permit, a Social Security card and a driver’s license.
“This is heartbreaking for me,” Joshua Aviles said. “I don’t know how I can mentally continue working 12+ hour days knowing that my dad is somewhere, possibly being treated like a criminal.”

Asked to confirm whether Luis Manuel Aviles had a Social Security number, a work permit or pending immigration cases, as his family indicated, DHS told Telemundo, NBCUniversal’s Spanish-language network, that “work authorization or a pending application do NOT confer legal status in the United States.”

The Lincoln left its home port of San Diego on Nov. 25, and, with more than eight months since it visited a port in December, it broke the Navy record for time without a port call. Relatives of sailors on board the carrier have described reports of deteriorating conditions and morale. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has said claims about the situation on board have been “completely misrepresented.”
The Navy said Saturday that the Lincoln has officially left the Middle East en route to the West Coast, a journey that could take a month or more.
Joshua Aviles, who told NBC News he has limited internet access, wrote on Facebook that he’s doing everything he can to get his father released from detention.
“I love you with all my heart. Please stay strong. I’m coming home, Dad,” he wrote.

President Donald Trump has stood by his administration’s immigration crackdown, including ICE’s expanded enforcement and arrests, which in recent months have included the arrests of children and spouses of service members, a San Diego Padres minor-league catching coordinator and a grandmother from India who’s a schoolteacher with a green card.

Immigration authorities have detained more than 50 parents and spouses of service members during Trump’s second term, according to a recent Associated Press investigation. There has been backlash to the detentions, which come despite programs for military members that can sometimes offer immediate family protection from deportation.
The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services website says those “discretionary options” are offered on a “case-by-case basis.”
It was not immediately clear whether Luis Manuel Aviles was in the program.
The DHS spokesperson said in a statement Sunday that “having a family member in the military is not a free pass to violate our nation’s laws.”
“Military service by an immediate relative does not automatically grant parole, lawful status, or immunity from immigration enforcement,” the spokesperson said.
Delgado lamented that her stepbrother has spent nine months out at sea, without seeing his family, “and this is what his father gets.”

title: Dan Sullivan endorses Dan Sullivan to beat Dan Sullivan in perplexing Alaska Senate race
summary: A third Dan Sullivan — a former Anchorage mayor — has weighed in on the competitive Senate race, endorsing Sen. Dan S. Sullivan over former teacher Dan J. Sullivan.
story: A new Dan Sullivan has entered the conversation surrounding the Alaska Senate race, in which incumbent Dan S. Sullivan faces a candidate with the same name.
The Republican former mayor of Anchorage, Dan A. Sullivan, endorsed GOP Sen. Dan S. Sullivan for re-election over retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan and Democratic former Rep. Mary Peltola on Tuesday.
“As the OG Dan Sullivan, I urge Alaskans to vote for Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. He’s been great for Alaska,” the former mayor wrote on Facebook.

Both Dan S. Sullivan and Peltola advanced to the general election in November after the all-party primary last week. The primary is decided by ranked-choice voting, and the top four finishers advance, regardless of political affiliation. NBC News has not yet made a call regarding who the other two candidates will be, but Dan J. Sullivan could be among them.

Alaska’s Senate race is considered one of the most competitive this cycle, when control of the upper chamber hangs in the balance. With primary votes left to count, Peltola so far has 48% of the vote, with Sen. Dan S. Sullivan taking 43%. Dan J. Sullivan — who is running as a Republican — has 2.4%, with other candidates getting considerably fewer votes.
Democrats view the election as a seat they could flip in November. The Cook Political Report rates the race a tossup.

The Sullivan saga has drawn attention as former teacher Dan J. Sullivan’s candidacy has faced legal challenges. Dan S. Sullivan and Republicans have alleged that the teacher was placed on the ballot to confuse voters and detract from the senator’s share of the vote, claiming he’s working with Peltola.
Dan J. Sullivan has denied coordinating with the Peltola campaign. Peltola has also denied any involvement with the second Sullivan campaign.

The Alaska Supreme Court ruled last month that Dan J. Sullivan can stay on the ballot after the state Division of Elections originally disqualified him. NBC News has reported that state and federal prosecutors in Alaska were investigating whether the race could be part of a conspiracy to confuse voters. A grand jury issued subpoenas this month to compel information from witnesses linked to Dan J. Sullivan’s campaign.

title: 5 people and multiple animals killed on rural Oregon property, with suspect found dead
summary: A suspect in the killings of five people whose bodies, and those of several animals, were found on a rural property in Oregon was found dead Sunday, officials said.
story: A suspect in the killings of five people whose bodies, and those of several animals, were found on a rural property in Oregon was found dead Sunday, officials said.
The Washington County Sheriff’s Office identified Benjamin Charles Parker, 36, as the suspect in the “complex investigation.”
“Officers from the Enumclaw Police Department located Parker’s vehicle and found him deceased inside,” the sheriff’s office said Sunday. “It is believed he died by suicide.”
Enumclaw is a small city in Washington state.

Detectives do not believe the quintuple homicide was random, according to the sheriff’s office. Washington County Sheriff Caprice Massey said they believe Parker “was known to the subjects,” in remarks Sunday night.
Officials initially responded Saturday morning to a 911 call about a vehicle fire in unincorporated Washington County, outside the city of Forest Grove.
Washington County Sheriff’s Detective Shannon Wilde said at a news conference Sunday that they are trying to confirm the identities of the victims.
Wilde said the “large scene” is on a rural property with some other homes around and “a lot of vegetation.”
Massey said, “I will say that in my 22 years here, I have not been a part of or witnessed a scene quite this complex involving this type of an investigation.”
There is no continued threat to the public, according to the sheriff’s office.
Forest Grove is about 25 miles west of Portland, Oregon, and 190 miles southwest of Enumclaw.

title: French tourist dies in Death Valley heat after vehicle gets stuck in mud
summary: The temperature reached 116 degrees the day Pierre Michel Formosa, 68, died, the National Park Service said.
story: A French tourist died last week in California’s Death Valley after the vehicle he was in got stuck in mud and he ventured away for help in temperatures that reached 116 degrees, officials said.
Pierre Michel Formosa, 68, was with a companion Monday when the vehicle they were using got stuck in mud, the National Park Service said Friday in a news release.

The two set out on foot along the desert salt flats toward the paved Badwater Road, one of the park’s main roadways, to seek help, it said. Formosa said he couldn’t keep going and stopped about 1.3 miles into the trek, according to the park service.
The companion made it to the road and flagged down a driver at about 2 p.m., it said, triggering a search for Formosa that included park rangers and a California Highway Patrol helicopter.
Searchers found Formosa’s body that afternoon, about 1.5 miles from Badwater Road, the park service said.

Death Valley National Park Superintendent Mike Reynolds offered condolences to Formosa’s family. “This is a heartbreaking reminder of how quickly conditions here can turn dangerous,” he said in a statement.
The location of Formosa and his companion’s vehicle is near a hiking trail in a historic mining area, according to the independent archive of the park service.

The National Weather Service issued an extreme heat warning for the area through Sunday night, warning of “dangerously hot conditions.” High temperatures in Death Valley were expected to remain in the 115- to 118-degree range Monday and Tuesday, with a high of 119 expected Wednesday.
The park service urged visitors to stay on paved roads during times of extreme heat, carry satellite phones or beacons and have plenty of drinking water on hand.
“Death Valley is an extraordinary place,” Reynolds said, “but its heat, distances, and remoteness can be dangerous, regardless of experience.”

“Military service by an immediate relative does not automatically grant parole, lawful status, or immunity from immigration enforcement,” the spokesperson said.
Delgado lamented that her stepbrother has spent nine months out at sea, without seeing his family, “and this is what his father gets.”

title: Sean Grayson, ex-deputy convicted of fatally shooting Sonya Massey, dies, attorney says
summary: Grayson was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer in 2023, one of his attorneys said previously. It was unclear if that is what caused his death.
story: Sean Grayson, the former Illinois sheriff’s deputy convicted of fatally shooting Sonya Massey in her home in 2024 after she called 911 to report a prowler, has died, his attorney said Sunday.
Daniel Fultz, the attorney who represented Grayson during his murder trial, said he died around noon. He was six months into his 20-year sentence for second-degree murder.

Grayson, 32, was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer in 2023, and it had progressed to Stage 4 and spread to his liver, lungs and rectum, another defense attorney, Mark Wykoff, said at his sentencing in January. In July, he was denied medical release by the Illinois Prisoner Review Board.
It was not immediately clear whether cancer is what caused Grayson’s death.
Grayson shot Massey, 36, after he responded to her 911 call shortly before 1 a.m. July 6, 2024. The shooting, which was captured on body camera video, set off protests and calls for justice.
Grayson was convicted last year.
During the 911 response, Massey picked up a pot of boiling water from her stove, prompting Grayson to back away, according to court testimony.
Grayson testified that he believed Massey was going to throw the boiling water on him after she said, “I rebuke you in the name of Jesus.” When Grayson looked confused, Massey repeated the sentence.
He testified that he took the remark as a threat.
Grayson pointed his gun at Massey and threatened to shoot her, according to body camera video. She apologized and dropped to the floor, but he fired three times, striking her.
Grayson declined to offer medical care, Sangamon County State’s Attorney John Milhiser said in court. Massey was pronounced dead at St. John’s Hospital in Springfield.
First Assistant State’s Attorney Mary Beth Rodgers said in court: “‘I’m sorry.’ That is the last thing Sonya Massey said before the defendant murdered her, just like he said he would.”
Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker signed the Sonya Massey Act, a law requiring stricter background checks for law enforcement hires, and it went into effect at the beginning of the year.
Sangamon County officials agreed in early 2025 to pay a $10 million settlement to Massey’s family.

story: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called steep new U.S. tariffs on a wide swath of his country’s goods “a miscalculation” Saturday morning after trade talks with Canada collapsed late Friday.
Carney blamed the breakdown of talks on what he said were the Trump administration’s “uneconomic” and “unfair” demands.

The 50% tariffs affect about $20 billion worth of U.S. imports from Canada, according to the U.S. Trade Representative’s Office. The import taxes will hit everything from hockey sticks to some building materials, liquors and certain kinds of clothing.

Carney said Canada was pursuing a “focused response,” with tariffs on the U.S. “concentrated in sectors such as steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics.” The duties would take effect Sept. 8, he said.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Saturday morning in an interview on Fox News: “We don’t have new talks planned with the Canadians. We’ve said enough, and so we’ve taken countermeasures.” He also said the U.S. would “respond to Canadian retaliation.”
Kyle Kirkwood wins IndyCar race in downtown D.C. celebrating U.S. 250th birthday

Blasting down those iconic and bumpy streets with a view of the U.S. Capitol from his car, Florida native Kyle Kirkwood took the checkered flag to win a once-in-a-lifetime IndyCar race on a sunny Sunday.

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix was an elaborate 250-mile spectacle in Washington with few expenses spared to celebrate the country’s semiquincentennial, bringing the city a rare blend of power, money and speed.

Kirkwood, who races for Andretti Global, started second but took the lead on the opening lap with a daring maneuver around the outside of pole-sitter and championship leader Alex Palou in front of the National Archives. From there, he proved unbeatable.

Reaching top speeds of about 180 mph, the cars zipped down Pennsylvania Avenue between the Capitol and the White House, the longest straight on the track. They raced past the D.C. courthouse and the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum on the seven-corner track.
“You can’t even put it in words. This is incredible,” Kirkwood said in a postrace interview. “Man, that was a hard race. One hundred forty-seven laps. I’m out of breath right now.”

A fast-growing wildfire destroying homes in northwest Reno, Nevada, on Sunday was human-caused and uncontained, authorities said as they encouraged 90,000 people to evacuate. At least six people were injured.

The Hawk Fire began Saturday and quickly grew to 20 square miles as it spread across the Peavine Peak area of Humboldt–Toiyabe National Forest, where rugged foothills are ringed by homes and businesses near the California line.

The fire moved exceptionally fast Saturday night, jumping over fire trucks and making it difficult for responders to get to hot spots while residents were trying to get out, Washoe County Sheriff Darin Balaam said.

Several structures were destroyed, and the injured included three civilians and three first responders, officials said. They did not provide additional details about how the fire was started, saying it was under investigation.

Mark Ruffalo is pushing back against Paramount Skydance after the media giant characterized his anti-merger comments as antisemitic. Ruffalo called the accusation “appalling and fundamentally dishonest.”

The dispute traces to a social media post from the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions movement — a Palestinian-led campaign opposing Israel’s occupation, which began in 1967 — that Ruffalo had boosted.
The post featured comments from Oracle Executive Vice Chair Safra Catz describing the company’s assistance to Israel following the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack.

title: CeeDee Lamb’s home burglarized while Dallas Cowboys star was at training camp
summary: Evidence showed a single person entered and exited the home through a broken window in late July, authorities said.
story: Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb’s Texas home was burglarized in late July and $300,000 worth of property was stolen while he was at training camp, police said.
It’s the latest hit in a string of brazen burglaries targeting affluent athletes in recent years.
Police responded to Lamb’s home in Fairview, Texas, the afternoon of July 31 for a report of a home burglary.

When officers arrived, they met with “individuals representing Mr. Lamb” who showed them a broken window on the side of the home where the burglars most likely entered, Fairview police said in a statement Sunday.

Evidence pointed to a single person’s entering and exiting through that window, taking “several high-end personal items,” officials said. More than $300,000 worth of property was stolen, including four luxury bags, the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reported, citing the police report.
An investigation continues.
Lamb, 27, who was selected by the Cowboys in the first round of the 2020 NFL draft, was at training camp with the team in Oxnard, California, at the time of the burglary.
NBC News has reached out to Lamb’s representative for comment.
The burglary is yet another incident in a spate of break-ins targeting high-profile athletes’ homes.
Last month, Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley’s Pennsylvania home was invaded while he and his family were home, police said. No one was injured.

Last year, a 21-year-old Seattle man was charged in connection with burglaries at the homes of four current and former NFL and MLB players, including Seattle Mariners pitcher Luis Castillo and former Seattle Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman.

Also last year, three men alleged to be part of a theft group from South America were indicted in a break-in at Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow’s home. In that case, more than $300,000 in luggage, glasses, wristwatches and jewelry was stolen, according to the criminal complaint.

title: This is what you need (and need to do) to stay safe this hurricane season
summary: I talked to a meteorologist to find the best way to prepare for hurricanes and what products you should have on hand.
story: As a Florida native, I’ve endured a lot of hurricanes and I’ve seen the damage they can cause. If you don’t take proper precautions, the destruction hurricanes leave behind can be catastrophic. This is why it’s important to know how to prepare for a hurricane, and make sure you have all of the supplies necessary to keep you and your family safe. Storms have already started making their way across the United States, with tropical storm Lala impacting Hawaii earlier this week. Plus, a potentially record-breaking El Niño is growing in the Pacific ocean, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

Power outages, flooding, broken windows and damage to homes and cars from fallen trees are just some of the things you need to be ready for. And while you may have a generator in case the electricity goes out, it’s important that you know how to use it properly to avoid carbon monoxide exposure.

I talked to a meteorologist and professor at the University of Florida to learn what measures you should take to make sure your home withstands a storm, and the best emergency kits and other supplies you should always have handy during hurricane season.

How to prepare for a hurricane
There are many different ways to prepare your home ahead of a hurricane to prevent damage, and to keep everyone safe, particularly in the event that you lose power during and after the storm.

“If you live by the coast, you should be thinking about storm surge, rainfall, and wind speed,” says Stephen Mullens, a meteorologist and assistant instructional professor of meteorology at the University of Florida’s Department of Geography. “Most fatalities and property damage comes from flooding as a result of both storm surge (water that has been moved from the ocean onto land) and from too much rain during the storm.”
The below preparedness tips are key for dealing with common problems during a hurricane, including flooding, power outages, broken windows from strong winds and fallen trees.

Watch for an evacuation warning: “If you are by the coast, look up whether you are in an evacuation zone,” says Mullens. “If you must evacuate during a storm, you only need to travel just outside the evacuation zone.” State government officials will traditionally issue evacuation warnings at least a few days ahead of a hurricane if not more, depending on what category the storm falls under. Be sure to stay on top of news updates. “You will need to leave before the wind and rain arrives, so your home preparations must happen with a deadline in mind,” says Mullens.

Prepare for flooding: Flooding is not only dangerous and a threat to your safety, but it can also cause irreparable damage to your home, which, even with insurance, can be extremely costly to deal with. Mullens recommends using things like sandbags to blockade your home if possible. “These can help prevent water from seeping under [home] doors and garage doors. Most of the time, you won’t experience the worst-case scenario, and sandbags can really help when flooding is only a few inches,” says Mullens. “No amount of [sandbags] will allow you to stay in an evacuation zone [though]. If flooding is forecast to be more than a foot, then plan to evacuate in case the forecast gets worse or your emergency management deems evacuation to be mandatory.”

Mullens also recommends preparing other areas around your home for excess water, too. “Outside your home, clear your gutters and drainage areas of leaves and other debris,” he says. “You don’t want water backing up and pooling in ways you don’t expect.” If your home does get flooded, there is a very short window of time before it will cause mold growth and become a pain to handle, according to Mullens. “It’s a race against time to prevent the build up of mold in drywall and furniture. If your roof has been damaged, a large tarp will prevent future rain from entering your home,” he says. “Inside, fans and a lot of towels will help dry things out.”

Prepare for strong winds: “To prepare for wind, trim branches on trees and bushes so they won’t hit the house. Bring furniture and outdoor decorations inside,” says Mullens. “For large items, stake and tie them down or they will likely fly away. If you live near the coast, nailing plywood over your windows can prevent damage inside your home from flying debris.” Additionally, make sure your cars aren’t beside trees, especially ones with coconuts or large branches that could fall during the hurricane and damage the body, windows or windshields.

Keep electronics charged: Make sure all your electronics are charged before the storm arrives and be sure to stock up on batteries as needed for things like flashlights and other essential devices. “Charge phones while power remains,” says Mullens. “Write down important information in case your phone’s battery runs out before power is restored.” Depending on the severity of the storm, a power outage is very likely, even if it’s just temporary.

Gas generators are one of the most common appliances that people use to restore power in their homes during and after hurricanes, according to Mullens. If you don’t have or plan on using a generator, there are alternatives you can consider, too. Some batteries work for home appliances, not just small handheld electronic devices, according to Mullens. “Today, large batteries can power an air conditioner, well pump, refrigerator, oven, or microwave for several hours,” says Mullens. “It’s important to assess what you most want to have power during an extended power outage, your ability to store the unit when you don’t need it, and cost to guide your purchases.”

Prepare for a disruption in water supply: A loss in access to clean water is also a common issue during and after a hurricane, so it’s important to make sure you have a plan in case you don’t have water for a few days. “Buy large water jugs for drinking and sanitation. Fill them with water prior to a storm,” says Mullens. “You can also fill a bath tub with water so you can flush your toilets. Most storms won’t be the worst-case scenario, but if it does happen you will want enough water for drinking and food for seven days.”

Buy non-perishable foods: Since losing power is common during and after hurricanes, you won’t have access to traditional kitchen appliances like a refrigerator to keep food fresh, an electric stovetop and oven or microwave, unless you find batteries or power stations suitable for powering them. Be sure to buy shelf-stable foods that don’t require cooking or refrigeration after opening, including canned vegetables and soup, cereal, granola bars, chips and crackers. “All these items can be stored at room temperature for a year unless otherwise noted,” says Mullens. “In the summer, before hurricane season, purchase one to two of these items each shopping trip instead of right before a storm.”

This kit has more than 300 pieces, including several sets of adhesive bandages in multiple sizes and shapes, wound closure strips, gloves, an emergency blanket, a pill box, gauze, wipes and a thermometer.

The kit comes in a rectangular, waterproof bag with a zipper closure and handles for easy carrying. It’s small and weighs less than 2 pounds, so it fits in some glove compartments and backpacks. Its compact size and take-anywhere design is a standout for people who bought it.

It’s connected to emergency radio channels so you can stay aware of weather updates, including from the NOAA, according to the brand.

It has a flashlight and tactile (not digital) buttons that adjust the volume and change the channel. Plus, it has an antenna and an automatic siren that turns on to let you know when severe weather is coming, according to the brand.
Frequently asked questions

It’s extremely important to not wait until the last minute to buy emergency hurricane supplies, since options will be very limited. Be sure to prepare for the most common problems, like flooding, lack of access to fresh water (including for your toilet), fallen trees and branches and power outages, says Mullens. You can do this by buying things like non-perishable foods, bottled water or gallons of water, medication, power stations and making sure your electronics (including your phone) are fully charged.

Since hurricanes often lead to power outages, you should stock up on things that being without power would affect, Mullens. This includes getting multi-gallon water jugs from stores like Home Depot, Lowe’s or Amazon so you can keep a large supply of water. You should also buy non-perishable foods that don’t have to be refrigerated, including canned foods and dry pantry items. Lastly, you should also stock up on energy by charging all of your portable devices, including a portable power station, and have enough batteries for emergency devices like flashlights.

Yes. While hurricanes are definitely a threat to coastlines, areas far from coasts aren’t exempt from experiencing their effects. Additionally, trailers and mobile homes are particularly vulnerable to damage from hurricanes, according to Mullens.

"Trailers and mobile homes are lighter and more likely to be damaged than homes built on a foundation. Thinner walls mean debris thrown in the wind are more likely to damage walls and windows,” says Mullens. “Being lighter means wind and flood water is more likely to lift the home off its supports. There may be less to do inside and outside to prepare the home itself, but you will likely need to evacuate earlier than recommended.”

While generators are a great appliance when it comes to providing a lot of power during a hurricane, they also can be dangerous when used improperly because they can expose you to carbon monoxide, according to Mullens.

"If you are using a gas-powered generator, the unit must be placed outside with cords running from the generator into the house. It is very common for people to operate generators indoors or in a garage, resulting in the resident dying due to a build-up of carbon monoxide,” he says. “If you are using a large battery, you may want to incorporate solar panels or another method to recharge it in case of an extended outage.”

title: Sean Grayson, ex-deputy convicted of fatally shooting Sonya Massey, dies, attorney says
summary: Grayson was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer in 2023, one of his attorneys said previously. It was unclear if that is what caused his death.
story: Sean Grayson, the former Illinois sheriff’s deputy convicted of fatally shooting Sonya Massey in her home in 2024 after she called 911 to report a prowler, has died, his attorney said Sunday.
Daniel Fultz, the attorney who represented Grayson during his murder trial, said he died around noon. He was six months into his 20-year sentence for second-degree murder.

Grayson, 32, was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer in 2023, and it had progressed to Stage 4 and spread to his liver, lungs and rectum, another defense attorney, Mark Wykoff, said at his sentencing in January. In July, he was denied medical release by the Illinois Prisoner Review Board.
It was not immediately clear whether cancer is what caused Grayson’s death.
Grayson shot Massey, 36, after he responded to her 911 call shortly before 1 a.m. July 6, 2024. The shooting, which was captured on body camera video, set off protests and calls for justice.
Grayson was convicted last year.
During the 911 response, Massey picked up a pot of boiling water from her stove, prompting Grayson to back away, according to court testimony.
Grayson testified that he believed Massey was going to throw the boiling water on him after she said, “I rebuke you in the name of Jesus.” When Grayson looked confused, Massey repeated the sentence.
He testified that he took the remark as a threat.
Grayson pointed his gun at Massey and threatened to shoot her, according to body camera video. She apologized and dropped to the floor, but he fired three times, striking her.
Grayson declined to offer medical care, Sangamon County State’s Attorney John Milhiser said in court. Massey was pronounced dead at St. John’s Hospital in Springfield.
First Assistant State’s Attorney Mary Beth Rodgers said in court: “‘I’m sorry.’ That is the last thing Sonya Massey said before the defendant murdered her, just like he said he would.”
Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker signed the Sonya Massey Act, a law requiring stricter background checks for law enforcement hires, and it went into effect at the beginning of the year.
Sangamon County officials agreed in early 2025 to pay a $10 million settlement to Massey’s family.

title: French tourist dies in Death Valley heat after vehicle gets stuck in mud
summary: The temperature reached 116 degrees the day Pierre Michel Formosa, 68, died, the National Park Service said.
story: A French tourist died last week in California’s Death Valley after the vehicle he was in got stuck in mud and he ventured away for help in temperatures that reached 116 degrees, officials said.
Pierre Michel Formosa, 68, was with a companion Monday when the vehicle they were using got stuck in mud, the National Park Service said Friday in a news release.

The two set out on foot along the desert salt flats toward the paved Badwater Road, one of the park’s main roadways, to seek help, it said. Formosa said he couldn’t keep going and stopped about 1.3 miles into the trek, according to the park service.
The companion made it to the road and flagged down a driver at about 2 p.m., it said, triggering a search for Formosa that included park rangers and a California Highway Patrol helicopter.
Searchers found Formosa’s body that afternoon, about 1.5 miles from Badwater Road, the park service said.

Death Valley National Park Superintendent Mike Reynolds offered condolences to Formosa’s family. “This is a heartbreaking reminder of how quickly conditions here can turn dangerous,” he said in a statement.
The location of Formosa and his companion’s vehicle is near a hiking trail in a historic mining area, according to the independent archive of the park service.

The National Weather Service issued an extreme heat warning for the area through Sunday night, warning of “dangerously hot conditions.” High temperatures in Death Valley were expected to remain in the 115- to 118-degree range Monday and Tuesday, with a high of 119 expected Wednesday.
The park service urged visitors to stay on paved roads during times of extreme heat, carry satellite phones or beacons and have plenty of drinking water on hand.
“Death Valley is an extraordinary place,” Reynolds said, “but its heat, distances, and remoteness can be dangerous, regardless of experience.”

title: 5 people and multiple animals killed on rural Oregon property, with suspect found dead
summary: A suspect in the killings of five people whose bodies, and those of several animals, were found on a rural property in Oregon was found dead Sunday, officials said.
story: A suspect in the killings of five people whose bodies, and those of several animals, were found on a rural property in Oregon was found dead Sunday, officials said.
The Washington County Sheriff’s Office identified Benjamin Charles Parker, 36, as the suspect in the “complex investigation.”
“Officers from the Enumclaw Police Department located Parker’s vehicle and found him deceased inside,” the sheriff’s office said Sunday. “It is believed he died by suicide.”
Enumclaw is a small city in Washington state.

Detectives do not believe the quintuple homicide was random, according to the sheriff’s office. Washington County Sheriff Caprice Massey said they believe Parker “was known to the subjects,” in remarks Sunday night.
Officials initially responded Saturday morning to a 911 call about a vehicle fire in unincorporated Washington County, outside the city of Forest Grove.
Washington County Sheriff’s Detective Shannon Wilde said at a news conference Sunday that they are trying to confirm the identities of the victims.
Wilde said the “large scene” is on a rural property with some other homes around and “a lot of vegetation.”
Massey said, “I will say that in my 22 years here, I have not been a part of or witnessed a scene quite this complex involving this type of an investigation.”
There is no continued threat to the public, according to the sheriff’s office.
Forest Grove is about 25 miles west of Portland, Oregon, and 190 miles southwest of Enumclaw.

title: Minnesota man charged in death of co-worker crushed by hydraulic grapple in prank gone wrong
summary: The man is accused of saying he was trying to make the shadows look like a truck’s grapple had his co-worker’s head but didn’t realize where it was before he closed the claw.
story: A Minnesota man is accused of crushing his co-worker’s head with a hydraulic grapple while the pair were “f------ around” during a tree-trimming job, killing the 26-year-old co-worker.
Christopher Boone Crimmins, 34, is charged with second-degree manslaughter, accused of operating a truck-mounted hydraulic grapple that closed on his co-worker’s head.

According to a criminal complaint filed Friday in Dakota County, Crimmins told police that he and Tyler Anthony Lynch, 26, were working together in Apple Valley on Thursday afternoon when the two started “f------ around.”

The men noticed the grapple’s shadow and Lynch’s shadow on the ground, and Crimmins began moving the grapple to make it look like it was grabbing Lynch, the complaint says. Crimmins was watching the shadows rather than Lynch himself, it says, and didn’t realize the grapple was closing in on Lynch’s actual head until it crushed it.
Police found Lynch on the ground “with a large amount of blood around his body and a significant injury to his head,” according to the Dakota County Attorney’s Office.

A witness told investigators they saw the grapple hit or pinch Lynch’s head, the complaint says. Crimmins was the only member of the crew with the commercial license to operate the machine, which the team was using to clear branches.
Bail was set at $40,000 unconditional or $20,000 with conditions, the county attorney’s office said Friday.
Crimmins faces up to 10 years in prison if he is convicted.

Crimmins was not listed in Dakota County Jail records Sunday afternoon. Court records were not immediately available, and it’s unclear whether he has an attorney. There was no immediate response at a phone number listed for him Sunday.
He is next expected in court on Sept. 10, according to the county attorney’s office.

title: Tim Scott calls support for Darline Graham an ‘easy choice’ despite her debate flub
summary: In an interview with “Meet the Press,” Scott defended Graham after her recent debate blunder raised questions about her qualifications.
story: Sen. Tim Scott defended Sen. Darline Graham, his fellow South Carolina Republican, on Sunday ahead of her special GOP primary runoff this week, dismissing concerns about her debate blunder on national security last week.
“Darline Graham is the real deal,” Scott told NBC News’ “Meet the Press,” adding that she is “highly qualified, incredibly competent, ready for primetime.”

Asked how confident he is that Graham will win Tuesday’s primary runoff, Scott said, “Very confident,” adding that he waited several weeks before he endorsed her “to make sure that I felt like she was ready.”

“I can tell you, as the senior senator for the great state of South Carolina, the person I want in the Senate with me, Darline Graham, representing the people of South Carolina,” he said. “Easy choice.”
Scott boosted Graham just days after her viral moment at a debate against Rep. Ralph Norman, R-S.C., whom she faces in Tuesday’s runoff.

Asked whether Taiwan and the South China Sea are important national security issues facing the U.S., Graham answered: “I’m just going to be honest here. I’m not, on national security, I’m not that informed on national security, so, but I do support the military.”

She added: “My brother was in the Air Force for 33 years, so I will do everything I can to support the military. My dad was in the Army. I’m not a polished politician up here. National security is not my thing, not my area of expertise. But I do support the military.”

The answer drew concerns from some Republicans about Graham’s readiness to govern on national security and foreign policy issues — which were of pre-eminent  concern for her brother, the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C. — if she’s elected to a full term.

Darline Graham was appointed last month to serve the rest of her brother’s term after he died unexpectedly. Several days after she was appointed, Graham decided to run in a special election to serve a full term and was quickly endorsed by President Donald Trump. After the special primary election, in which Graham and Norman advanced to a runoff, Scott endorsed her, as well.

Trump and Scott rallied in South Carolina in support of Graham’s campaign Friday, with Trump telling voters: “She only knows how to put America first. ... You vote for her, you’re going to be very proud of that vote.”

On Sunday, Scott, who is chair of the Senate Republicans’ campaign arm, the National Republican Senatorial Committee, also spoke about competitive general election contests in states like Texas, Michigan and Iowa coming up in November.
He defended the NRSC’s rhetoric about Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who would become the first Muslim senator if he is elected.

The NRSC has repeatedly referred to El-Sayed’s faith in social media posts and alleged he has “terrorist ties” despite the lack of any evidence for the claim, drawing criticism from Democrats that Republicans are inciting Islamophobia.
In an interview on “Meet the Press” this month, El-Sayed responded to GOP attacks painting him as “too radical,” saying, “We always knew they were going to go here.”
“At the end of the day, it’s not radical to believe that people should be able to afford their groceries. It’s not radical to believe that you should have healthcare in this country,” he said.

“Now, they’re going to try and paint me as a certain thing, given my name, but I also think it’s important for us to recognize that America has a long history of embracing,” he added. “America is a lot bigger than very small people.”

Scott on Sunday pointed to El-Sayed’s decision to campaign in the primary with Hasan Piker, a Twitch streamer who once apologized for comments he made about the U.S. deserving the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks.
“Birds of a feather flock together,” Scott told “Meet the Press.” “The company you keep does matter.”
Scott added that even though El-Sayed has denounced Piker’s past comments, he has not said he would stop campaigning with him.
“You can’t denounce it with your words and do something different with your actions,” Scott said. “We believe what you do, not just what you say.”

Speaking about the Senate race in Texas, which is a competitive contest between GOP state Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democratic state Rep.  James Talarico, Scott denounced Talarico as “weird” and “radical.”

He also demurred when he was asked about concerns about Paxton’s character and his past, which includes an investigation by the Justice Department into whether he abused his office to aid a political donor and a 2023 vote by the GOP-led Texas House to impeach him. Paxton, who denied any wrongdoing and said the allegations were politically motivated, did not face any charges following the Justice Department investigation, and he was acquitted in a state Senate trial following his impeachment.
Scott, who endorsed Paxton’s opponent, Sen. John Cornyn, in the GOP primary this year, did not respond when he was asked whether Paxton has the character to serve in the Senate.

Instead, he denounced Talarico, saying: “I can tell you this: What we know with great clarity is that James Talarico does not have the character to serve in the United States Senate, nor does he have the ... right position on the issues that Texans care most about. I’ll say it very clearly, and I’ll say it again: James Talarico is out of step, completely out of step with Texans.”

Talarico has called the GOP attacks a distraction aimed at drawing attention from the allegations against Paxton, and he has emphasized his legislative record and what he said was a focus on bipartisanship as a state lawmaker.

“I’ve served for four terms in the Texas House of Representatives, where I brought Democrats and Republicans together to pass 60 bipartisan bills to cut property taxes, to raise teacher pay, to lower the cost of housing, childcare, prescription drugs, including insulin, and I’ve called out the extremes in both parties,” he said in an interview with NBC News in May.

title: Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he is ‘kicking the tires’ on a potential 2028 presidential bid
summary: The Maryland Democrat also said on “Meet the Press” that democratic socialists have a place in the party “as part of the debate.”
story: Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., said in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press” that he’s “kicking the tires” on a potential 2028 presidential bid.

“We need to be against the status quo, and that’s why I’ve been kicking the tires as I look at 2028, because I don’t think the Democratic Party has answered the call about how we’re going to make sure we have an economy that really does work for everybody, especially working people,” he said.

Van Hollen’s comments came as he was pressed about whether he is interested in challenging Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., as the chamber’s party leader, if Democrats retake the Senate this fall.
Asked by moderator Kristen Welker whether he was interested in the position, Van Hollen said his focus was “not on majority leader, it’s on what Democrats stand for going into 2028.”

Van Hollen, a longtime member of Congress, has been a prominent critic of the Trump administration and has pushed Democrats to provide a clear alternative to the Republican Party’s agenda. He has previously said he is “kicking the tires” in considering a potential 2028 run, acknowledging the possibility of a presidential campaign to NOTUS and at the Hill Nation Summit, an annual event put on by The Hill and NewsNation.

Asked to clarify on “Meet the Press” whether his “kicking the tires” comments meant he was thinking about running, he noted that he has been to New Hampshire and Iowa, which have historically been the first two nominating states. In 2028, New Hampshire will still be an early nominating state, but Iowa was pushed out of the early window.

“I think there’s a great deal of churning within the Democratic Party, and I support that,” he said. “As I said, I think we need this healthy debate, because I don’t think Democrats have put forward a clear alternative to the Trump administration.”
Pushed again about whether he was considering running for president, he said, “Democrats need to be very clear not just what we’re against, but what we’re for.”
“I very much want to be part of that debate, and I am kicking the tires, testing the waters,” he said.
Several other Democrats have appeared open to running for president in 2028 in what could be a wide field of candidates, with no clear potential front-runner.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom has said he would be “lying” if he denied he was considering a presidential campaign. Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear has said he may “take a look” at running. Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg said in an interview on “The Diary of a CEO” podcast that he doesn’t know whether he will run but that he is “more inclined than not.” Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., has said she hasn’t “ruled out the possibility.” Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., also has not ruled out a run, and Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., said he would “have to look at” the possibility. Former Vice President Kamala Harris, too, has said she is “thinking about” running for president again.
Van Hollen was also asked on “Meet the Press” whether he believes democratic socialists should have a place in the Democratic Party. He said, “They do, as part of the debate.”

“I’m not afraid to debate,” he added. “I think that those in the Democratic Party who are afraid of a healthy debate are missing the point because voters, including Democratic voters, they don’t want to simply return to the pre-Trump status quo. They want Democrats who are going to stand for something, and I can strongly disagree with one set of Democrats. But I think that debate is healthy.”

Multiple democratic socialists have won primaries this cycle, most recently Angie Nixon, who won the Florida Democratic primary for the Senate last week. Nixon is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, a group whose platform includes replacing “the president and Supreme Court with an executive and judiciary chosen by and subordinate to Congress” and abolishing the Senate.
Asked whether those platform points went too far for him, Van Hollen said, “Of course.”
“Yes, of course they do for me, and I think a lot of the folks who are running, regardless of where they are on the Democratic spectrum, have rejected those ideas,” he said.
Van Hollen served in the House for more than a decade before he was sworn in as senator in 2017.

title: Dan Sullivan endorses Dan Sullivan to beat Dan Sullivan in perplexing Alaska Senate race
summary: A third Dan Sullivan — a former Anchorage mayor — has weighed in on the competitive Senate race, endorsing Sen. Dan S. Sullivan over former teacher Dan J. Sullivan.
story: A new Dan Sullivan has entered the conversation surrounding the Alaska Senate race, in which incumbent Dan S. Sullivan faces a candidate with the same name.
The Republican former mayor of Anchorage, Dan A. Sullivan, endorsed GOP Sen. Dan S. Sullivan for re-election over retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan and Democratic former Rep. Mary Peltola on Tuesday.
“As the OG Dan Sullivan, I urge Alaskans to vote for Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. He’s been great for Alaska,” the former mayor wrote on Facebook.

Both Dan S. Sullivan and Peltola advanced to the general election in November after the all-party primary last week. The primary is decided by ranked-choice voting, and the top four finishers advance, regardless of political affiliation. NBC News has not yet made a call regarding who the other two candidates will be, but Dan J. Sullivan could be among them.

Alaska’s Senate race is considered one of the most competitive this cycle, when control of the upper chamber hangs in the balance. With primary votes left to count, Peltola so far has 48% of the vote, with Sen. Dan S. Sullivan taking 43%. Dan J. Sullivan — who is running as a Republican — has 2.4%, with other candidates getting considerably fewer votes.
Democrats view the election as a seat they could flip in November. The Cook Political Report rates the race a tossup.

The Sullivan saga has drawn attention as former teacher Dan J. Sullivan’s candidacy has faced legal challenges. Dan S. Sullivan and Republicans have alleged that the teacher was placed on the ballot to confuse voters and detract from the senator’s share of the vote, claiming he’s working with Peltola.
Dan J. Sullivan has denied coordinating with the Peltola campaign. Peltola has also denied any involvement with the second Sullivan campaign.

The Alaska Supreme Court ruled last month that Dan J. Sullivan can stay on the ballot after the state Division of Elections originally disqualified him. NBC News has reported that state and federal prosecutors in Alaska were investigating whether the race could be part of a conspiracy to confuse voters. A grand jury issued subpoenas this month to compel information from witnesses linked to Dan J. Sullivan’s campaign.

title: Hakeem Jeffries and Jared Kushner meet in NYC to discuss how Democrats and Trump could cooperate
summary: The meeting comes with just months to go before midterm elections that will determine control of Congress for the remainder of Trump’s term.
story: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., recently met privately with Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and informal adviser, and they discussed possible areas of cooperation, a source familiar with the meeting confirmed to NBC News.
The private meeting, which was first reported by The New York Times, took place in Manhattan, the source said.

The meeting was an unusual instance of a top Democrat and a close Trump confidant coming together to discuss common ground. Jeffries, the top Democrat in the House, is one of Trump’s most prominent critics. Meanwhile, Kushner is a close relative of Trump’s and has taken on a slate of high-profile foreign policy issues as special envoy.
The source, who was granted anonymity without being authorized to speak about the private meeting, did not share details about when it took place or what was discussed.

The Times reported that it happened “in recent weeks,” citing five sources with knowledge of the meeting. The Times also reported that the pair discussed “housing, immigration and the high cost of living,” citing two sources with knowledge of the meeting. The meeting space in New York was “offered up by a mutual friend of the two men,” the newspaper reported, citing two people with knowledge of the meeting and a third who was briefed on it.

Jeffries said in a statement Sunday that Republicans have adopted a “my-way-or-the-highway approach” that he said Democrats have made it clear “will not work and will be met with forceful opposition.”

“In every conversation that we have with the Trump administration, we will continue to make it explicitly clear that the affordability crisis is not a hoax and nothing short of transformational policy change is acceptable. We are fighting for an affordable America. The question is whether Republicans will join us,” Jeffries said.
The White House did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for comment on the meeting.

Despite their different policy perspectives, Jeffries and Kushner previously joined forces to champion a criminal justice reform bill during Trump’s first term. Kushner championed the bill, which Jeffries signed on to as a co-sponsor, giving it a bipartisan boost. The legislation, dubbed the First Step Act, was signed into law in 2018.

The recent meeting, though, comes as both parties are entering the final stretch of the campaign season before midterm elections, when Democrats hope to flip the House and the Senate. If Democrats flip even a single chamber, it could significantly stymie any future legislative initiatives from the administration.

If Democrats take back the House majority in November, Jeffries is the favorite to become the next speaker. He has predicted victory in the midterm elections, and he and his committee leaders have vowed to conduct aggressive oversight of the Trump administration on a range of issues, including ICE tactics, Trump’s Qatari-donated jet, his family business dealings and the White House ballroom.

Kushner remains a close confidant of Trump. He was a senior adviser in the White House during Trump’s first term, and he is currently special envoy for peace missions, focused largely on the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war, along with another special envoy, Steve Witkoff.

title: Karoline Leavitt to work for Trump-affiliated super PAC after leaving White House
summary: Press secretary Karoline Leavitt will work for President Donald Trump’s super PAC MAGA Inc.
story: Press secretary Karoline Leavitt will work for President Donald Trump’s super PAC MAGA Inc. after she leaves her post at the White House, she said Friday.

Leavitt, 28, told reporters aboard Air Force One that she will return to work for the super PAC, for which she served as a spokesperson before joining Trump’s 2024 campaign, though she did not specify what her new title will be.
MAGA Inc. did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Leavitt’s new role.

Speaking briefly in the press cabin before takeoff, Leavitt told reporters that she will miss the job “but I love my kids even more.” Leavitt added that she and her family will remain in Washington for a while, telling reporters, “You guys will still see me all the time.”

She told reporters that Friday’s flight to South Carolina for a rally supporting Sen. Darline Graham will be her last trip as press secretary, but that she’ll be back on board for the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention scheduled for Sept. 9 and 10.
Leavitt, who became the youngest press secretary in history when she joined the second Trump administration, announced her departure from the White House on Aug. 12.
Trump wrote in a Truth Social post that day that Leavitt was stepping down to “spend more time with her beautiful young children and family.”

The president added that Leavitt “will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party, as we work to defy History, and conclusively win the Midterm Elections.”

Leavitt, who gave birth to her second child in May and returned from maternity leave on July 16, wrote in her own post on Aug. 12 that she “felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary.”
Leavitt worked as an assistant White House press secretary during Trump’s first term before she became the communications director for Rep. Elise Stefanik, R-N.Y.
Leavitt then ran for Congress in New Hampshire, losing to Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas in 2022. She subsequently began working as a spokesperson for MAGA Inc.

After joining Trump’s 2024 campaign, Leavitt gave birth to her first child and returned to work just four days into her maternity leave in the wake of the assassination attempt against Trump at a rally in Butler, Pennsylvania.

As Leavitt leaves her role after 18 months on the job, she will become the second-longest-serving press secretary under Trump after now-Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders, who served in the role for almost two years during Trump’s first term.

title: Jenna Posts New Family Photos from Summer Trip: ‘August Slipped Away’
summary: Jenna Bush Hager shared photos from her family vacation on Instagram, including one shot with her daughters, her mom, Laura, and her sister, Barbara.
story: Jenna Bush Hager is squeezing every drop of summer she can before it comes to an end.
The TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle co-host posted a carousel of pictures from her family vacation on Instagram on Aug. 23.
“I can see us lost in the memory August slipped away into a moment in time,” she captioned the photos, quoting lyrics from Taylor Swift’s song “August.”

The first image brought together multiple generations of the Bush family. It captured Jenna with her mother, former first lady Laura Bush, along with twin sister Barbara Bush and her daughter, Cora, as well as Jenna’s daughters, Mila, 13, and Poppy, 11.
Barbara and husband Craig Coyne also share son Edward, 2, while Jenna and husband Henry Hager are also parents to son Hal, 6.

Other shots showed Jenna laughing with husband Henry Hager, kids frolicking on rocks near the water, the family on the beach together, kids walking through a garden, Jenna taking a selfie with Poppy and Jenna having a laugh.
Jenna often shares photos of sweet family memories. For the Fourth of July, she posted a roundup of pics of her family soaking up time at the beach and on a boat, captioning it, “Magic of July.”
While Jenna seems to have gotten plenty of quality time with her kids this summer, she’s previously reflected on how her children will become more independent as they grow up.

“I realized that I’m not going to be in all of my kids’ memories. And that actually is a great thing,” she said in 2024 at a TODAY Mother’s Day event. “They’re starting to become really independent, and they don’t need me as much. And I’m like, ‘OK, I did something right.’”

title: Leslie Mann Shares Brutally Honest Secret To Her 30-Year Marriage With Judd Apatow
summary: Actor Leslie Mann has opened up about how she’s been able to keep her three-decades-long marriage to director Judd Apatow going strong.
story: Actor Leslie Mann has opened up about how she’s been able to keep her three-decades-long marriage to director Judd Apatow going strong.
On an Aug. 20 episode of podcast “Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce,” Mann, 54, revealed the key to the superstar pair’s marriage.
“Just accepting how hard it is and not trying to fool yourself,” Mann told host Kylie Kelce. “That’s the secret.”
She also got real about just how difficult a lasting relationship can be.

“When I see other people talking about their perfect marriages or like how they never fight or they’re I don’t know, just all the the stuff that I can’t relate to ... That’s a red flag,” Mann said on the podcast.
Mann — who’s currently promoting comedy “Spa Weekend,” which hit theaters Aug. 21 — shares two daughters, Maude Apatow and Iris Apatow, with the director. The two have been married since 1997.
She first met Judd Apatow while she was auditioning for 1996 film “The Cable Guy.” In a 2017 interview with TODAY’s Willie Geist, Mann shared that for Apatow, it was love at first sight.

“He did say to Ben, ‘There goes the future, Mrs. Apatow,’” Mann said, seemingly referencing the film’s director Ben Stiller. “But I think he may have said that about Heather Locklear and, like, J Lo too.”
While on the recent podcast, Mann told Kelce that while the couple has their tiffs, she and Apatow, 58, still have a valuable connection.
“We find each other entertaining and funny — sometimes,” Mann said. “He is my best friend and I tell him everything.”
She added, however, that Apatow may not always reciprocate.
“I don’t know if he tells me everything. It comes out at certain times, and then sometimes he, like, shuts it down,” she said, before agreeing with Kelce that “it’s a universal man thing.”
Ultimately, Mann said, the relationship is an “important” one.
“You have a witness to your life also,” Mann said of marriage. “So your kids, growing all the memories — that’s important. That’s a that’s a big one.”

Mann and Apatow have not only been romantic partners, but they’ve also shared a professional relationship as collaborators. Beyond “The Cable Guy,” The pair have worked on “Knocked Up” and “Funny People,” “This is 40” and much more.
In a 2012 interview with Elle, Apatow said that Mann was a critical reason why he began to write better roles for the women in his projects.

“Leslie would always say, ‘There aren’t good roles for women, the female parts aren’t developed, the women are serving the men,’” he told the outlet. “And just seeing the stack of scripts she had to read showed me how little effort was put into making great female characters.”

title: People Are Divided On Margaret Qualley’s ‘Barefoot Sandals’ Red Carpet Look
summary: Actor Margaret Qualley, who’s currently promoting the upcoming Ridley Scott film “The Dog Stars,” stepped onto the red carpet at the film’s world premiere Aug. 20, wearing a pair of Chanel’s “shoeless shoes.”
story: The internet isn’t toe-tally sure if these are hot or not.

Actor Margaret Qualley, who’s currently promoting the upcoming Ridley Scott film “The Dog Stars,” stepped onto the red carpet at the film’s world premiere Aug. 20, wearing a pair of Chanel’s “shoeless shoes.” The look instantly went viral for its controversial aesthetic, with some loving the high-fashion shoes and others saying that they weren’t shoes at all.

The shoes, part of Chanel’s Resort 2027 collection, consist of black heels that are strapped to the feet with two sets of laces. There isn’t much of a sole. So when wearing these shoes, the majority of the wearer’s feet are bare and touch the ground.

The internet wasn’t quite sure what to make of the moment. One social media user on X joked that the shoes were just a reflection of “shrinkflation.  And another jokingly predicted that next season, the fashion brand will likely “sell the front part.”
However, there were still a number of people who were living for it. A social media user wrote, “chic this chic that. THIS is chic, to me”
Another person also described the shoes as “kinda chic high key.”

The shoes have been drawing a lot of opinions since they debuted on the runway in April at a show in the French seaside resort city of Biarritz.  At the time, Chanel’s creative director Matthieu Blazy, had already sparked debate for the design. And fashion insiders weren’t even united in their stances.
“Is it half the price as well?” one person wrote on Instagram.
Another described the shoes as an “updated anklet for the beach!”
So where do you stand on these haute couture shoes?

title: From Música Mexicana to Country, Carin León Is Making His Own Rules
summary: Mexican singer-songwriter Carin León has forged his own path when it comes to música Mexicana. Most recently he is dipping his toes into the American country space.
story: Authenticity is among Carin León’s core values, whether it’s with his music, clothes or way he carries himself.

That’s why the 37-year-old Mexican singer-songwriter has forged his own path when it comes to música Mexicana. Known for his banda and norteño roots, León isn’t afraid to dabble in different genres, most recently dipping his toes into the American country space.

His latest album, “MUDA,” is a mix of what audiences have grown to love from León’s contemporary sound, along with salsa, pop and country music. He’s previously described the project as a “representation of my unfulfilled musical desires.”

“I love regional Mexicano, obviously, but at the same time when I was a kid I was listening to rock music to rap music, a lot of R&B, soul,” León tells TODAY.com, alternating between Spanish and English. “This combination of genres and combination of ideas, it’s very interesting for me to mix all of those things and get to this whole new style in the way of my singing, making music and dressing.”

León has dominated Latin charts for years, with a dozen No. 1s on the Regional Mexican Airplay chart along with several No. 1s on the Latin Airplay chart. He’s also won four Latin Grammys and two Grammy Awards. He’s proving that the crossover is very much alive and well as he ventured into the country and soul space with collaborations with Kane Brown, Cody Johnson and Leon Bridges.
In 2025, he worked with Kacey Musgraves on the Spanglish hit “Lost In Translation.” He also teamed up with Jelly Roll on “Lighter,” a song featured on the official FIFA World Cup 2026 album.

On working with Musgraves, León says it’s wonderful to collaborate with artists “who have inspired” me. He also teases that, specifically in the country genre, he has “a lot of surprises” with “interesting” stars coming up.

While artists like Bad Bunny, J Balvin, Karol G and others have light up the global airwaves with reggaeton hits, León is making his presence seen in places that regional Mexican artists haven’t typically touched.
He’s performed at the Nashville’s Grand Ole Opry, known as one of country music’s biggest stages, and became the first Latin artist ever to perform at both Coachella and Stagecoach in the same year.

Currently on his “De Sonora Para El Mundo” North American tour, he’s partnered with Mexican beer brand Victoria to give fans the chance to win a custom limited-edition Cobija jacket, created by Mexican American designer Brenda Equihua, as well as a trip and tickets to one of his shows.
Inspired by his last name León, which translates to lion, the brown and tan jacket has the face of a lion stitched on the back. The artist says he wants one for himself to match with the lucky fan.
Up next, León is making history as the first Latino artist to headline Sphere in Las Vegas. The artist will perform at the iconic venue for two weekends, Sept. 4-6 and Sept. 11-13.

“It’s a whole different production because (the venue is) an amazing tool for us to express a lot of things that we can’t express regularly in a show,” he says, describing the creative process and production as a “dive into my brain.”
“See the world through my eyes, that’s the whole concept of Sphere,” he says. “How I see (my home state) Sonora, how I see my music, how I see the world through the eyes of a little boy from Sonora.”

León and his team have been preparing for his Sphere shows for about a year and a half. He attended a Backstreet Boys show to see Sphere in action, saying, “I’m such a fan of music. It (blew) my mind away.”
“I started to shake because I’m gonna be there,” he says. “It’s a stage that you have to respect. I’m very excited at this moment more than nervous.”
Whether it comes to music or his Mexican vaquero (cowboy) aesthetics he says in Spanish: “Las reglas son para quebrarlas,” which translates to, “The rules are meant to be broken.”

As he continues to break the mold of what a regional Mexican artist should look like, León says the most fulfilling moment so far this year is realizing that the risks he took have been worth it and accepted by fans.
“At first with my music, with the way I dress — I was scared to do it my way because it was different,” he says. “And I thought I would be punished by my audience or my fans.”
He adds that the “most important thing is to be real and authentic and when you lose that fear (of being criticized), that is the best thing that can happen to an artist.”

title: Love Jimothy? Meet Meemers, The Adorable Cat With Short Spine Syndrome
summary: For fans of the perfectly imperfect Jimothy the Raccoon, there’s now another furry friend over which we can all obsess.
story: For fans of the perfectly imperfect Jimothy the Raccoon, there’s now another furry friend over which we can all obsess.

Readers, meet Meemers: The adorable rescue cat who has short-spine syndrome, the same condition that Jimothy is also believed to have. The two-and-a-half-year-old feline, who’s based in Bloomington, Illinois, recently went viral for her barely-there neck and resemblance to Seattle’s beloved raccoon. One video of Meemers, posted Aug. 18, has drawn more than 41 million views as of Aug. 22.

Owner Katie Dahlen, who previously worked at the shelter where Meemers was found, has always loved making clips for social media. But, Dahlen tells TODAY.com, that she never expected the video of Meemers to go viral seemingly overnight.

“I missed making videos, and I was like, ‘Well, I have this awesome cat, and I want to share her with people,’” Dahlen says. “I just didn’t realize how big she would blow up in a 24-hour span. It was crazy.”
In the video, Meemers, in her black, fluffy glory, simply sits down. There’s a few shots of Meemers giving her best Blue Steel as well. And it’s truly easy to see why she’s so beloved.
“Sensational whiskers / body tea / no notes 🖤” one fan replied.
Another demanded a collab between Meemers, Jimothy and Tilly, the famous pup who also has short spine syndrome.

Meemers is certainly unique. From her shoulders to the base of her tail, she’s only about seven-and-a-half inches long. She also has a slight tail deformity. For Dahlen, who’s had Meemers for over a year now, it was love at first sight.

“She was actually left at the shelter in a box outside,” Dahlen says of the shelter at which she was working at the time. “Literally, from the day she came in, I was like, ‘She needs to come home with me.’”
Meemers was, at first, not in the greatest shape, Dahlen says. The fur around her butt was matted and there was an abscess in the area as well, Dahlen explains.

“The owner had tried to shave her, so you could tell they cared, but maybe they didn’t have the resources, and they were embarrassed about walking her in through the doors,” Dahlen says. “So they left her out front.”
After Meemers was given a course of antibiotics and some TLC, she was ready to head home with Dahlen. And since July 2025, Dahlen said she and her husband have been enjoying their adorable cat.

Given her deformities, Meemers has had to make a couple of adjustments in order to thrive, Dahlen says. She doesn’t climb much and she’s unable to jump. Because her organs are squished in her very small body, she needs to be held a certain way, Dahlen says. The feline also overheats quite easily.

“I always equate her to being kind of like a pug, where she overheats easily if it’s too warm outside,” she says. Dahlen adds that if Meemers over-exerts herself, she’ll start panting. “So a lot of her supervised outside time in her backyard is in the evening when it’s cooler.”
Dahlen points out that Meemers has “virtually no neck,” so she’s unable to successfully groom her own back. That’s where Dahlen comes in.
